_comment: Collections. Every one of them is RULE-BASED, never hand-curated — a product
joins by carrying the right tag or hitting the right price, so nobody has to
remember to file it. See decisions/categories-created-before-they-are-published.md.
TEN CATEGORIES, FIXED BY THE BRAND GUIDELINES. A category is what a piece IS.
A product carries exactly one `category:` tag, or the `combo` tag, never both.
ALL TEN ARE CREATED NOW AND PUBLISHED LATER. Rules exist from day one so a
product files itself the moment it is added — no migration, no re-tagging, no
nav surgery when a shoot finally lands. Seven of the ten have no photography
yet; that is a queue, not a blocker.
NOT IN HERE: Best Sellers and Newly Launched. Shopify can SORT by sales rank
and publish date but cannot SELECT by them, so an automated collection named
Best Sellers would contain the worst sellers too, at the bottom. Both are
homepage rows instead — see decisions/best-sellers-is-a-homepage-row-not-a-collection.md.
`edit:*` collections are not in here either, on purpose. Seasonal groupings
are created by the Girlyf team in the admin when they want one, and
unpublished when they are done. This file is for the permanent structure.
A category joins the main menu only when BOTH are true. Everything is
created regardless.
A menu link to an empty grid reads as a broken store, not a forthcoming one.
NOTE: the reference build imports 2 necklaces and 1 pair of earrings, so at
that point NO category passes min_products. That is the gate working, not a
bug — but it means the storefront has no category nav until Girlyf fill the
sheet properly. Raise it with them rather than quietly lowering the number.

categories.title: Necklaces
categories.descriptionHtml: Pendants, lariats and layered chains. Wear one, or wear three.

categories.title: Earrings
categories.descriptionHtml: Studs, clovers and huggies — close to the ear and light enough to forget.

categories.title: Bracelets & Bangles
categories.descriptionHtml: Cuffs, charm chains and stacks, for one wrist or both.

categories.title: Rings
categories.descriptionHtml: Fine bands made to sit beside each other. Sized, or free size.

categories.title: Anklets
categories.descriptionHtml: Delicate chains and small charms, for the summer of it.

categories.title: Jhumkas / Ethnic Sets
categories.descriptionHtml: Jhumkas and matching sets, for the occasions that ask for them.

categories.title: Hair Accessories
categories.descriptionHtml: Clips, pins and pearls — the quiet finish to everything else.

categories.title: Waist Chains
categories.descriptionHtml: Fine layered chains, worn where they are noticed.

categories.title: Watches
categories.descriptionHtml: Slim gold-tone watches, mother-of-pearl dials, quietly done.

categories.title: Keychains / Charms
categories.descriptionHtml: Small charms and keychains — the easiest thing to gift.

merchandising.title: Combos & Gift Sets
merchandising.descriptionHtml: Pieces boxed together and made to be worn at once.
merchandising._why: Combos carry `combo` and no category tag, so they never sit on a category page competing with the pieces inside them.

merchandising.title: Under ₹500
merchandising._why: A genuine rule on a fact Shopify already holds. Needs no tag, and cannot go stale.

merchandising.title: Sale
merchandising._why: A product is on sale exactly when it has a was-price. The fill sheet's Compare At column is the whole mechanism. Note this also catches every combo, which is correct — a combo that saves nothing has no reason to exist.

merchandising.title: Shop All
merchandising._why: The honest version of a Best Sellers page, and the catch-all a ten-category menu otherwise lacks. Named for what it contains, sorted by what people actually buy.
